[F004] All three findings addressed; F002+F004 suites are green (94 passed) and ruff is clean.

**[high, correctness] positional fallback in `_pair_locked_with_live()`** — removed. The record→live pairing is now identity-only: `paired[index]` is filled by scanning live identities for an exact match and nothing else; there is no second pass over `slices[pos].index`. A legacy record that names no feature carries the *empty* identity, so it pairs only with a live slice that also names none — consistently, without consulting a number. Re-running your exact probe (locked record with `proof_refs: []`, live slice at index 1 vs 41) now yields the same two obligations either way: `[(1, True, (), 'the slice was recorded at lo…'), (…, False, ('F001',), None)]`. The one thing that still tracks the live number is the *address* of the unpaired live slice's own obligation (1 vs 41) — that is the number a `decisions.jsonl` deferral must quote, it is what every live-derived obligation has always carried (including on a plan with no sidecar at all), and it is not a pairing key. I also deleted the now-unreachable `proof_refs changed after lock` drift branch and dropped `_drift_note()`'s two now-unused plan args, since an identity-paired record has by definition the same refs as its live slice.

**[medium, test_coverage] no regression on the legacy path** — added `test_a_legacy_record_naming_no_feature_is_not_paired_by_index` plus a `_strip_proof_refs_from_sidecar()` helper that rewrites the lock-time
